articleTitle: Credit Card Fraud Detection - Machine Learning methods
abstract: Credit card fraud refers to the physical loss of credit card or loss of sensitive credit card information. Many machine-learning algorithms can be used for detection. This research shows several algorithms that can be used for classifying transactions as fraud or genuine one. Credit Card Fraud Detection dataset was used in the research. Because the dataset was highly imbalanced, SMOTE technique was used for oversampling. Further, feature selection was performed and dataset was split into two parts, training data and test data. The algorithms used in the experiment were Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Naive Bayes and Multilayer Perceptron. Results show that each algorithm can be used for credit card fraud detection with high accuracy. Proposed model can be used for detection of other irregularities.

articleTitle: Recognition of stress levels among students with wearable sensors
abstract: Stress is an inevitable part of student life. The intense pressure of achieving high grades, maintaining a social life, dealing with financial obligations while away from family home present challenges that college students must deal with every day. This puts a huge amount of pressure on passing every exam in written form or during the presentation. Timely recognition of stress can be helpful to individuals by providing them with different stress- coping mechanisms. Wearable sensors allow for real-time monitoring of students physiological signals that can be closely related to stress. In this paper, we have monitored ten students with wearable sensors in order to recognize the stress levels experienced by students during exams. Features of the electrocardiogram and electro dermal activity signals were used as input to different classification methods. Obtained results indicate recognition accuracy between 86-91% for three classes, including relax state, written exam, and oral exam.

articleTitle: Preservation of Cultural Heritage Sites using IoT
abstract: Religious/historical buildings ought to be preserved for as long as possible. The ancient structures themselves and the rich collections they store represent irreplaceable wealth for future generations. They also provide the space for the customs and traditions to sustain. In addition, cultural heritage sites can stimulate economic growth but need to be maintained as well. This paper proposes an effective and affordable solution for the monitoring of preservation conditions of the Church belonging to Eastern Orthodox cultural heritage. The solution is based on utilization of modern Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) and services with general structure and main design principles using the three-layer IoT architecture. This research is an ongoing work only involving the first step towards realization of preservation monitoring system.

articleTitle: Application of low-cost VL53L0X ToF sensor for robot environment detection
abstract: In this paper usage of a small, light, low-cost VL53LOX sensor for robot environment detection is proposed. Using the time-of-flight technology it provides reliable information about surrounding objects over a range of up to 2 meters. Precision of the sensor is tested using surfaces of different materials and colors. Also sensor operation under different lighting condition was tested. It is shown that this sensor provides a good and reliable low-cost alternative that has potential application in robotics for the purpose of proximity sensing and potential applications in object recognition and odometry.

articleTitle: Mechatronics, Identification Tehnology, Industry 4.0 and Education
abstract: Computing infrastructure is an ever-changing category which influence of technology advancements is so obviously that can be see almost on daily level. This influence is very important especially in the fields of Mechatronics and Identification technology in creating environments for introducing concept of Industry 4.0. One of the approaches to overcoming this difference in the speed of the process in education and production / services is continuously improving curricula with a particular emphasis on the introduction of identification technologies as one of the main features of the concept Industry 4.0. In this paper are described some of the experiences in applying this approach to study programs carried out at the Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad and College of Information and Electrical Engineering, China Agricultural University.

articleTitle: Performance analysis on Android SQLite database
abstract: Database performance is a very important factor in the development of any application. Some applications need very fast feedback, others process a large amount of data and without the support of modern database management systems, this is almost impossible. In this paper main focus is to analyze SQLite Android relational database management system and test its performance in several scenarios: dealing with CRUD operations on unencrypted data, encrypted data, as well as concurrent access to the database. For this purpose, an application that demonstrates performance impacts on the SQLite database has been developed and published on the Google Play Store. Testing results show that operations over encrypted data take much longer than on unencrypted data. Furthermore, it is shown that a new SQLite locking and journaling mechanism provides concurrency with an efficiency of 40-44%.

articleTitle: Monitoring System Based on IoT Sensor Data with Complex Event Processing and Artificial Neural Networks for Patients Stress Detection
abstract: The stress level has been recognized as one of the key factors in the determination of life quality of the individuals. The sensor data obtained by testing patients to various stress levels are very important in order to understand better the circumstances that lead to elevated stress. This paper gives a description of the possible system capable of complex event monitoring of sensor data. The dataset used supplied the stress levels of several patients. The artificial neural network was created for the classification of stress levels and its results can be further used in an IoT system with complex event processing capabilities.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Power MOSFET Reliability and Failure Modes
abstract: In this study, based on the characteristic parameters of MOSFET's degradation, reliability of MOSFETs from different companies has been compared. Same type of MOSFETs are investigated. Acceleration test are designed and devices are degraded. According to degradation data, transfer characterization is investigated and failure modes of MOSFETs have been examined. This degradation data of values have been observed %10 variance which is degradation's sign.

articleTitle: BER Calculation for Sweep Jamming of MPSK Modulated RCIED Activation Message Signals
abstract: This paper presents the development of the method for accurate BER calculation when MPSK modulated RCIED activation message is jammed using sweep signal. The derived formulas are achieved for QPSK, 8PSK and 16PSK modulated signals jamming. It is proved that BER tends to maximum value 0.5 when jamming signal power increases and that only 20% lower BER value is obtained for less than 7dB higher jamming signal level than it is the level of RCIED activation signal. These results point out that it is not necessary to apply too high emission power to achieve acceptable jamming effect. As a consequence, jammer practical implementation is easier and its dimensions are smaller.

articleTitle: Line arresters and underbuilt wire application in lightning protection of 110 kV and 220 kV overhead transmission lines
abstract: Lightning strikes are one of the most frequent cause of overhead line outages. To reduce backflashover rate of critical lines special lightning protection system must be applied. In this paper application of line arresters and underbuilt wire on 110 kV and 220 kV overhead transmission line are analyzed. Efficiencies of applied lightning protection systems are estimated through the numerical calculations performed in the EMTP-ATP software. It is concluded that both line arresters and underbuilt wire can provide high level of line lightning protection. Installation of underbuilt wire at overhead line provide better lightning protection efficiency than installation of one line arrester per tower, except in case when tower footing grounding resistance is extremely high.

articleTitle: An Improved Version of Student Attendance Management System Based on RFID
abstract: Student attendance registration is one of the routine but time-consuming tasks of teaching staff at higher education institutions. Various technical solutions are implemented to alleviate the administrative burden and partly automate this task. Most of them include the use of one or more of the following - Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology, biometric solutions such as fingerprint and face recognition and mobile devices - mostly smartphones. In this paper, we present an improved version of our system based on RFID and some results of its use in a real environment. The main improvements have been made to a hardware component RFID reader and to a web-based application that is used by the faculty staff. Besides the usual features of similar systems related to student attendance, the system also includes features that enable integration with external systems, recording of necessary data regarding the work of teachers in class and generating of periodical reports on their work.

articleTitle: Reducing energy costs by using optimal electric vehicles scheduling and renewable energy sources
abstract: Nowadays companies can reduce their energy costs by using renewable energy sources, storage devices and optimized scheduling of charging/discharging of electric vehicles (EVs). This paper analyzes the influence of the number of EVs, photovoltaic production and daily variations of buying/selling prices on the reduction of energy costs. This problem is solved by power management and optimized scheduling of EVs charging/discharging, taking into account the intermittent behavior of renewable energy sources and vehicles demands for charging. Company savings are achieved by minimizing the costs of purchased energy from the main grid, by selling the energy from renewable energy sources and optimized scheduling of EVs charging/discharging. In this paper the costs are minimized by using optimization in Lingo.

articleTitle: An implementation of a deeply programmable SDN switch based on a hybrid FPGA/CPU architecture
abstract: Software-Defined Networks (SDN) simplify tasks performed by the network switches and centralize the network management by clearly separating networking processes into an application, control, and data plane. An OpenFlow, the flagship of SDN implementation, has reduced the innovation of such networks by diminishing switching tasks to the simple lookup of packet flow tables. A novel hybrid architecture of a deeply programmable packet-switching node (DPPSN), based on field-programmable gate array (FPGA) and central processing unit (CPU) technologies, is proposed, with the aim of overcoming OpenFlow's limitations regarding the ability to implement new protocols and advanced packet processing functionalities. It has been demonstrated, through the implementation and experimental evaluation of the DPPSN, that it is justified to use hybrid FPGA/CPU architecture for this purpose.

articleTitle: Use of Integer Genetic Algorithm for Optimal Allocation and Sizing of the Shunt Capacitor Banks in the Radial Distribution Networks
abstract: This paper deals with algorithm for placement and sizing of the shunt capacitor banks in distribution networks of radial structure. In this paper algorithm for optimal placement and sizing of shunt capacitor banks is based on load flow calculation algorithm and integer genetic algorithm. Firstly, paper describes the problem of optimal placement and sizing of the shunt capacitor banks with constrains. Also, paper describes algorithm for the calculation of the load flow in the radial distribution networks. Used integer genetic algorithm is also presented. Proposed algorithm was verified on the IEEE 34 bus test distribution network. Finally, practical application of the proposed algorithm was demonstrated on one real 10 kV distribution network in Bosnia & Herzegovina.

articleTitle: An IoT Solution for Secured and Remote Sound Level Monitoring
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of an Internet of Things (IoT) application that performs the sound level monitoring. The phonometer used for sound level measuring is connected on Arduino MEGA combined with ESP8266 WiFi module. The data transfer to the PC (client) is provided over Raspberry Pi server. The implementation is done using MQTT protocol.

articleTitle: Prediction of self-excited vibrations occurance during aluminium alloy AL 7075 milling
abstract: Despite the existence of other production methods, metal cutting still plays an important role in modern production. The performance of machine tools has a decisive role in terms of productivity and quality of production increase. When we are talking about improving the performances of machine tools, the analysis of the appearance of self-excited vibrations and their isolation take a significant place. The aim of this paper comes from trends and limitations that are present in metal production. The paper presents analytical and experimental methods for identifying stability lobe diagrams in the aluminum alloy Al 7075 milling. The influence of certain regime on the occurrence of self-excited vibrations, i.e. the definition of vibrational stable processing regimes, is considered.

articleTitle: Implementation of High-Availability Server Cluster by Using Fencing Concept
abstract: Contemporary business-technical challenges require the implementation of advanced security techniques and the reliability of applications and services. Distributed computer systems allow access to powerful computing resources and are often based on server clusters and advanced virtualization techniques. This paper presents one solution for the implementation of high-availability server ceph cluster using the Proxmox open source virtualization platform. The Intelligent Platform Management Interface (IPMI)-based fencing technique has achieved an enviable level of reliability of virtual machines running on the cluster. It has been shown that the implementation of open source virtualization solutions, a properly designed server cluster, and advanced fencing techniques can significantly improve the reliability and availability of services and applications.

articleTitle: Effects on LEDs during the Accelerated Ageing Test
abstract: The advancement of LED technology in the last 10 years has completely put other light technologies into the fore-ground. LED has almost entered all spheres of life. When it comes to products that use LED technology, one of the most important issues is lifetime. This paper contains a detailed overview of the research in the field of lifetime testing of LED components and products which have an LED element. Mathematical models for accelerated LED ageing tests are given in this paper. Ageing tests with constant temperature and constant current were analyzed. In this paper a simplified model of the lifetime of LEDs in products is proposed. The results of testing several samples for a product with an LED based technology are given.

articleTitle: Thermal Imagery Noise Influence on Face Recognition Performance
abstract: The utilization of a thermal band imaging sensor with aim to overcome the disadvantages of visible light face recognition systems, such as variation in lighting conditions, has become more popular in wide range of security and safety applications. Thermal imaging sensor enhances reliability of face recognition systems under different lighting conditions, including complete darkness. However, thermal imagery also possesses several disadvantages such as usual presence of noise, originating both from sensor and environment. This paper examines the influence of thermal imagery noise on face recognition performance in thermal-to-thermal face recognition applications.

articleTitle: File system performance comparison in full hardware virtualization with ESXi and Xen hypervisors
abstract: This paper focuses on the hypervisor type-1 performance comparison, taking into consideration VMWare ESXi and Citrix XenServer platforms. The hypervisors performances are evaluated through filesystem performance testing procedures. For both of the hypervisors, the testing procedures are performed under the same conditions. We have applied Filebench benchmark tool, which guarantees equality and independent of the influence of any hardware or system characteristics. As the guest operating system we have chosen CentOS 6.3 Linux distribution. We have compared native ESXi and Xen hosts performances, for systems with one, two and tree virtual machines. Initially, we have provided hypotheses related to the expected behavior and validated them with the results.

articleTitle: Comparison of Feature Descriptors for Visible and Thermal Face Recognition
abstract: Face recognition, as one of the biometric methods, in controlled environments reaches recognition accuracy of more than 99%. Regardless of that, variations in lighting conditions, pose, facial expressions and occlusions result in performance degradation. Including thermal infrared facial images in face recognition systems can provide a solution to these problems, especially for limitations caused by illumination. Both thermal and visible face recognition systems can use the same, common image processing feature descriptors. This paper compares the two most common feature descriptors, HOG and LBP, and examines their performance both in visible and thermal face recognition applications in order to find more effective feature descriptor for each image sensor.

articleTitle: Power Flow for Distribution Network with Renewable Energy Sources
abstract: The power flow techniques are of great importance for the modern distribution network expansion planning due to the increasing uncertainty. In this study, a probabilistic power flow is proposed in order to incorporate long-term uncertainty sources which are load demand, wind speed, and solar irradiance. A convolution-based power flow is constructed by using the matrices of the bus-injection to branch-current and branch-current to bus-voltage. Its results are compared with that of full AC power flow in terms of the accuracy. The results of bus voltages and current flows are obtained for radial 21 bus benchmark system and the obtained results show that the uncertainty related to renewable generation and load are incorporated into power flow problem effectively in terms of accuracy and required simulation time.

articleTitle: LCR of the Ratio of the Product of Two Squared Nakagami-m Random Processes and Its Application to Wireless Communication Systems
abstract: The paper takes into account second order statistics (SOS) of the ratio of the product of two squared-Nakagami-m (s-N-m) random processes (RPs). The obtained results can find their application in variety of wireless communication systems (WCSs). Mathematical apparatus has been developed for deriving fast computing, closed form, approximative expression for level crossing rate (LCR) using Laplace integration formula. The influence of s-N-m fading severity parameters for the proposed RP on the LCR is investigated and graphically presented for radio frequency (RF) WCS as well as optical WCS (OWCS) scenarios.

articleTitle: Optimal Capacitor Placement in Distribution Network for Loss Reduction and Voltage Profile Improvement
abstract: This paper presents a method for optimal multi objective capacitor placement in the medium voltage distribution network. The purpose of the proposed algorithm is to determine the optimal sites and sizes for capacitor installation in distribution network for power loss reduction and voltage profile improvements. The search for the set of candidate solutions is performed using an evolution inspired, multi objective genetic algorithm, while the conflict among candidate solutions from Pareto front is solved using the fuzzy multi criteria decision making based on Bellman-Zadeh method. In order to demonstrate its relevance, the problem is tested on the model of a real distribution system, currently operated in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The results indicate that Distribution System Operator (DSO) can benefit from optimal capacitor placement in distribution network. The proposed algorithm was proved to have a practical relevance as it can be applied to realistic distribution system. The presented results are relevant to the DSO for planning purposes, for customers because it has potential to lower the power distribution cost and finally for regulators who are overseeing the network planning and long term management process.

articleTitle: Control of Half-Bridge Resonant PWM Converter for Electromagnetic Vibratory Actuator
abstract: The subject of this paper is the control system of the half-bridge resonant pulse width modulation (PWM) converter for electromagnetic vibratory actuator (EVA). Although the half-bridge converter topology has been analyzed in the literature, mainly silicon controlled rectifiers (SCRs) have been employed as semiconductor switches, whereby the use of transistors would offer some advantages regarding effectiveness of control. Therefore, the main objective of this paper is to replace SCRs with transistors in the half-bridge resonant topology, and to develop a suitable control system for amplitude-frequency control of EVA. The switching instants of transistors in the half-bridge converter are determined in order to accomplish resonant operating condition of EVA, thus ensuring maximum amplitude of vibrations with minimum energy consumption. The amplitude of EVA vibrations and half-bridge converter switching instants are estimated by employing a state observer, resulting in a high performance feedback control loop. The effectiveness of the proposed control system is verified by computer simulations and the results are thoroughly discussed.

articleTitle: One approach for full-text search of files in MongoDB based systems
abstract: This paper presents an approach for full-text search of files stored in MongoDB database and GridFS system. This solution contains an API Rest interface that processes the requests and provides all business logic and MongoDB database that provides storage features. Besides, the simple web application has built to illustrate the usage of the system. The implemented solution has no dependency on any other full-text engine and it is implemented on its own. The proposed system can be integrated into any document management system or enterprise application system to provide the feature of searching content in stored files based on free form text.

articleTitle: Identification of Voltage Parameters of Dynamic Load Model on 35 kV Side of the Transformer
abstract: Modelling of voltage dependent load is always a current topic due to existence of an adequate load model is a prerequisite for calculation of steady states and the analysis of transient regimes of power systems. Given that it is important to know the load model parameters, we have performed the measurements in electric power system of Bosnia and Herzegovina (EPS BIH). The main idea is to identify the values of voltage parameters of dynamic load model. Therefore, this paper describes the dynamic load models and the methodology for exponential dynamic load model parameter identification. It also presents the voltage parameters of dynamic load model for a node in EPS BIH and compares them to similar published studies, concluding that the difference in given parameter values is the consequence of local load characteristics.

articleTitle: Design and Testing of High Voltage High Frequency Transformer 0.6kV/60kV for Power of 60kW
abstract: The paper presents the results of the development of high voltage high frequency (HVHF) power transformer 0.6kV/60kV, which is applied within a multiresonant power converter for supplying the electrode system of electrostatic precipitators (ESP). The design of HVHF transformer was the major challenge, since it was designed for a power of 60kW and a working frequency of ≈10 kHz. Before the integration with the HVHF multiresonant power converter, the transformer was laboratory tested in open-circuit and short circuit regimes. Further, complete thermal vision of the transformer was performed. Key results of the experimental verification, including characteristic waveforms and thermal images for the previously mentioned operating regimes, are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Centralized monitoring of the power electronics devices
abstract: This paper describes the solution for monitoring and control of power electronics devices in telecommunication facilities. Centralized monitoring of the power supply system enables monitoring of the operation of all devices in the system, using the same user application. In addition to monitoring of individual devices’ operation, the operation of passive elements, which together with the power electronics devices constitute the power system, is also monitored. With the implementation of derived alarms, such as organized, centralized monitoring increases the reliability of the power electronics system and enables the responsible sector to prevent interruptions in the operation of telecommunication equipment by preventive maintenance. Managing power electronics devices represents switching on or switching off of monitored devices or modules, starting a capacitive test, and adjusting the operating parameters of the power supply device from the remote monitoring center. It is estimated that with such organized remote monitoring, the total costs of installation and maintenance of the power system can be reduced by 16%. The cost resulting from the interruption of telecommunication traffic as well as the cost of termination of the services due to the unreliable operation of the telecommunication system is not included in the savings’ calculation.

articleTitle: Power transformer reliability assessment based on tap changer dynamic resistance and motor current measurements
abstract: Information about the remaining power transformer life and the condition of its components is the most important role of asset management. One of the main causes of transformer failure is on load tap changer. In this paper, consideration of the power transformer reliability with regard to the state of the on load tap changer, based on the dynamic resistance measurement and tap changer motor current will be given.

articleTitle: Performance of Self-Corrected Min-Sum Decoding Algorithm for Decoders with Quantized Input
abstract: In this paper we explore the Min-Sum decoding algorithm for LDPC codes with self-correction (SC-MS) modification and how it affects the error correction performance for quantized input data. Three levels of quantization are observed: 3-, 2- and 1-bit.It was shown that the self-corrected modification significantly improves the performance of Min-Sum decoding algorithm with quantized input in comparison with basic Min-Sum decoding algorithm. Convergence of the algorithm is also better than for basic Min-Sum algorithm.Results of error correction performance and convergence are presented for two codes: CCSDS (8176, 7156) and IEEE 802.3an (2048, 1723) LDPC. The results are also presented for the SC APP-based and basic Min-Sum decoding algorithms.

articleTitle: Inducing creativity in engineering education: a crowdvoting approach
abstract: This paper investigates creativity of students in the context of engineering education. The main goal is to get new insights on how to motivate engineering students to express more creativity in solving their assignments. The research included a crowdvoting contest on a sample of was 28 students in the area of information technologies at Faculty of Organizational Sciences, University of Belgrade. Results point out that a crowdvoting competition can be used to induce students' creativity in engineering education. Additionally, we discuss how students creativity styles relate to the design of creative-based educational tasks.

articleTitle: Automatic Text Summarization of News Articles in Serbian Language
abstract: Text Summarization is a technique of creating short, accurate, and fluent summaries of longer text documents or sets of documents. With growing amount of textual data circulating in the digital space, there is a need to develop machine learning algorithms that can automatically shorten longer texts and deliver accurate summaries. First, the generated summaries should fluently pass the intended messages. Second, the generated summaries should reduce reading time and speed up the process of researching for relevant information. By large majority, most of research in text summarization has been done for English texts. In this paper, we experiment with a variation on a graph-based method called TextRank for extractive text summarization. The dataset used in this study is collected from one of the online news sources in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

articleTitle: Mobile Phone Data visualization using Python QGIS API
abstract: Data visualization is a graphical representation which helps in unveiling hidden patterns from large and complex data, so called Big Data. The term Big Data is used for datasets which have wide, varied and transcendental structure and are thus challenging for storing, analyzing and visualizing. Logical interpretation is not possible from raw data, because people are visual by nature. Only thanks to the visualization, the human brain can process, absorb and interpret concurrently plenty of information. Due to the fact that creation of information is growing more rapidly than people's consumption of information and that there is an urgent need for utilization of that information in real time, the automatization of the processing and visualization data is mandatory. Here, we examined how to automatize process of visualization of CDR (Call Detail Record) data using open source Python QGIS API.

articleTitle: The effect of oversampling on the probability of false alarm in detection of noise-affected binary sequences
abstract: In this paper is presented the effect of oversampling on the probability of a false alarm in the binary sequences used in the process of synchronization in digital communication systems when only a noise is presented on the input of a receiver. Within this, it is evaluated the dependence of the probability of the false alarm on the binary sequence length, L, and the number of samples per bit, k. Although, the expression of the length of equivalent one-sampled sequence through which the effect of oversampling can be observed is derived. Finally, the results of the simulation and the measuring of the probability of the false alarm are shown in function of the number of samples per bit.

articleTitle: Students’ Success Predictive Models Based on Selected Input Parameters Set
abstract: Modern LMS systems offer many possibilities for adapting e-learning courses' teaching materials. In order to make the adjustment more efficient, many educational data should be analyzed. This paper describes one possible solution for evaluation of students' parameters available at the very beginning of the courses. Based on detected significant input parameters sets, students' success predictive models are created and key factors that can help prevention of dropping out and failing the course are identified.

articleTitle: Static Excitation of the 7.5 MW Synchronous Motor for Compressor Drive
abstract: In this paper, the static excitation system is presented, designed for a compressor implemented by means of the 7.5 MW synchronous motor. Advantages of the new digitally controlled static excitation system are outlined, together with all major control and protection functions that it includes. The response traces are presented, measured during the synchronous motor commissioning.

articleTitle: Software Based Analysis of Food Cooling Technology
abstract: Analysis of patent databases is becoming everyday practice since the developers of new products and services need to get the contemporary trends on defined topics of interest. In addition, companies analyze patent data and use collected information for defining future research and development plans and market strategies. As food storage device is one of the most arguable topics in the last decade, this paper shows qualitative and quantitative analysis of patent portfolio created on this topic using publicly available patent search engines. Conducted patent analytics can be used by all interested parties involved in different phases of food product life cycle.

articleTitle: Fractional model and analytically determined response of DC motor with separate excitation
abstract: In recent years, the use of DC motors has been constantly increasing, both in different home appliances and industrial drives. Some specific applications, such as robots and medical devices, require more advanced mathematical model of electrical machine that incorporates the physical effects that the standard model cannot take into account. Additionally, such models provide a more detailed dynamic analysis. In this paper, the fractional mathematical model, which is suitable for analysis of DC motor with separate and constant excitation, is derived. The model is formulated in the form of a system of fractional different equations. Furthermore, the transfer functions of the electrical and mechanical subsystems, as well as the transfer functions that describe dependence between the rotation speed and supply voltage and the load torque, are specified. Moreover, analytical solutions of certain subsystems and for complete DC machine are derived.

articleTitle: RTL-SDR Based Hardware-In-The-Loop Bit Error Rate Measuring System
abstract: Communication between two or more participants is obtained through a non ideal transmission medium. Such medium is usually characterised by different types of distortions which affect transmitted signal. Many of them are not completely avoidable. In order to minimize their effect at the receiver end, adequate performance measure of distortion-to-signal influence is needed. As the one of the most reliable measures for evaluating total distortion on transmitted signal, from transmitter to receiver end, we consider a bit error rate. In this paper, we propose a low-cost bit error rate measuring system constructed as RTL-SDR based wireless Hardware-In-The-Loop system. The proposed measuring system is tested in indoor environments on BPSK modulated signals. Obtained results show high matching with theoretical expectations. Also, for the proposed system adequate graphical user interface is created in the Matlab.

articleTitle: Benefits of using 5G Network Slicing to implement Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) technology
abstract: This paper presents an overview of V2X technology where 4G and 5G network slicing is applied. Network slicing enables multiple logical slice networks to be created over one physical network, where each slice can individually be managed and configured depending on different needs related to bandwidth, latency, privacy, QoS parameters etc. Using network slicing in V2X increases the possibility of creating smart and secure traffic where all information in traffic circulates flawlessly. V2X network slicing can be applied over cellular networks in 4G with LTE-A, but the arrival of 5G V2X network slicing will bring major improvements. The aim of this paper is to describe advantages of using 5G network slicing V2X in relation to 4G network slicing V2X.

articleTitle: Issues of Human Activity Recognition in Healthcare
abstract: Human activity recognition substantiates itself as a useful tool applicable in many smart assistive technologies. Gathering, evaluating, and analyzing data in order to recognize human activities poses many issues, especially in healthcare applications. This paper seeks to answer the question what are the issues regarding the human activity recognition process in healthcare. After conducting a review of approaches used to implement each stage of a specific activity recognition process, the results indicated that issues mostly arise in data collection stage. Based on that, the applicability of related approaches (i.e., wearables, smartphones, and non-contact sensing) is discussed. Underlying issues are identified in order to serve as a starting point for future research activities.

articleTitle: Application of the Quadrature Demodulation for the Measurement of Electric Power Parameters
abstract: Electric power can be divided into active, reactive and apparent power. The following parameters are used to estimate all types of electric power: power of fundamental spectral component, power of harmonics and the power in a given frequency band. To determine these parameters, the most effective method is based on the application of spectral analysis for voltage and current. The complex spectrum of signal is normally obtained using discrete Fourier transform or by quadrature demodulation. The quadrature demodulation technique allows a higher measurement accuracy. This article considers the application of quadrature demodulation for measuring complex spectrum, frequency, and power parameters. Analytical expressions of cross-correlation of the measurement errors and the parameters of the output filter are obtained. The application of moving average filter and a Butterworth IIR-filter as an quadrature demodulator output filter are considered. Simulation modeling was performed in Matlab.

articleTitle: The Influence of Task Complexity and Duration when Testing QoE in WebRTC
abstract: Web real-time communication (WebRTC) is technology enabling peer-to-peer communication with voice, video, messaging, and data sharing via browsers. WebRTC adoption depends on many influence factors (IFs) that affect quality of experience (QoE). Related research activities have indicated that context IFs (CIFs) are important to understand the QoE in WebRTC. The main objective of this paper is to understand the effect of task and temporal contexts (i.e., task complexity and duration) on QoE. Experimental study is conducted including survey with end users to collect mean opinion score (MOS) when performing the task of different complexity and duration in video calling over WebRTC. Analysis conducted by using statistical methods reveals the existence of statistically and practically significant effect of selected CIFs (i.e., task complexity and duration) and their interactions on QoE for video calling over WebRTC. The quantification of relationship between selected CIFs and QoE is proposed in form of prediction QoE model for video calling over WebRTC.

articleTitle: Time Series Prediction of Air Pollutants : A Case Study for Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Italy
abstract: Pollution levels are highly dependent on the meteorological parameters, as the weather conditions dictate pollution dispersion and concentration. With the rise of global environmental protection initiatives, there is also a need for accurate prediction of pollution levels. This paper presents a time series prediction of NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and CO given four meteorological parameters: (i) air pressure, (ii) relative humidity, (iii) average daily temperature, and (iv) wind speed, using a Nonlinear Autoregressive Exogenous (NARX) neural network. The research is a case study of three European countries: (i) Serbia, (ii) Bosnia and Herzegovina, and (iii) Italy, and involves data from 2014 to 2016 for a total of 1096 instances. The results show that the best prediction accuracy is obtained for CO for data regarding Italy and Bosnia and Herzegovina, and for NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> for data regarding Serbia. Moreover, the best predictor variables of NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> are air pressure and relative humidity, followed by the wind speed. The best predictor variables of CO are pressure and temperature for Bosnia and Italy, and wind speed for Serbia.

articleTitle: Near real-time data aggregation using foreign data wrappers from a network of sensors
abstract: In this paper a novel approach to distributed data collection within a large industrial plant consisting of many different automated and manual working nodes is presented. The data is collected from different sensors on many machines locally to a commodity IoT platform with local relational database storage and the collected data is shared and aggregated with other database systems utilizing concept of foreign data wrappers instead of industry standard SCADA. Alternative approaches were investigated and compared for inclusion in a larger management information system (MIS) for tracking production in near real-time locally and remotely. This way, a uniform virtually monolithic database for the MIS was implemented with much lower peer cost and greater security, reliability and availability. The data collected could be used for real-time visualization, reporting and long term analysis of the production monitored.

articleTitle: CIM-based integration in smart grids: Slovenian use cases
abstract: The paper presents basic concepts of integration and CIM-based data exchange in smart grids. It presents the scope of the problems which distribution network operators and transmission system operators are facing in todays' environment. Furthermore, the paper explains the need for interoperability within power systems operators and explains the standardization which is in place to serve these purposes. The IT integration standards are based on the IEC CIM (Common Information Model - family of standards IEC61970, IEC61968 and IEC62325) whose' main aim is to integrate the system operator's existing and newly introduces OT/IT systems by means of a common service-oriented architecture concept. Basic concepts and methodologies in such projects are given. This methodology is then demonstrated through multiple use cases which were implemented in Slovenia in the scope of the Slovenian-Japanese cooperation project - NEDO involving two local distribution network operators and the transmission system operator. A brief description of the project is given as well as results and conclusions.

articleTitle: Two Axes Electro-hydraulic Platform for Generating Stochastic Vibrations
abstract: From the point of view of the oscillatory comfort of cars, it is very important to study the transmission of vibrations through the human body and their influence on the psychophysical characteristics of men. In most cases of interest there are stochastic vibrations of the frequency band 1Hz-30Hz, but previous research in this field has shown that human beings are very sensitive to the frequencies less than 1Hz, such as 0.1Hz or even less (to about 0.05Hz). This paper presents the practical realization of a two-axis electro-hydraulic platform and corresponding control system for generating stochastic vibrations in order to examine the oscillatory comfort of truck seats. The control system is based on monitoring narrowband and broadband reference waveforms generated by the method of direct digital synthesis (DDS). The realized two-axis electro-hydraulic system can also be used for vibration testing of other loads up to 200kg in the frequency range 0.1-30Hz. The verification of the realized system was confirmed by the experimental results given at the end of the paper. The presented system was realized at the Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac at the Department for Motor Vehicles and Motors.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Distributed Computing Infrastructure in the VI-SEEM Project
abstract: In this paper we present an approach we have developed to monitor distributed and heterogeneous computing infrastructure with special attention to the implementation in the Virtual research environment for regional Interdisciplinary communities in Southeast Europe and the Eastern Mediterranean project (VI-SEEM). The project infrastructure covers a number of countries and administrative domains as well as several computing paradigms, from classic data center virtualization solutions to grid and high performance computing. We have collected and analyzed available data sources, designed data model and implemented the monitoring system suitable for monitoring of this complex infrastructure. To validate the proposed approach we have tested the system within VI-SEEM project and present the test results in this paper.

articleTitle: Electric vehicles utilization for peak demand control in modern distribution networks
abstract: Development of Electric Vehicles (EV) makes a huge step forward to complete transition from conventional fossil fuel driven vehicles to modern, renewable energy based vehicles. Integration of large capacity charging stations (CS), specially developed for plug-in electric vehicles, into smart grid concept of distribution system is analyzed in this paper. Electric vehicles are considered not only as controllable loads but also as significant resource for peak demand control. In that manner proposed optimization framework is developed and implemented using genetic algorithm. Proposed optimization procedure is tested on different case studies. Simulation results, together with proposed optimization framework and derived conclusions could serve as basis of different short-term planning studies or even for development of real time control algorithms.

articleTitle: Overview of Information Technology Knowledge and Skills Necessary for Contemporary Translation
abstract: In present time, the efficient, prompt and quality performance of any form of translation largely depends on different forms of knowledge and skills relating to the various aspects and uses of information technology. In other words, in the age of extensive use and overall availability of computers and the Internet, the “classic” manner of translation, implying the use of pen, paper, gained knowledge and dictionaries, has simply become obsolete, inefficient and time-consuming. After an introduction, dealing with the basic concepts and definitions relating to translation and interpreting, an overview of IT knowledge and skills which have become necessary for a contemporary translation will be given in the central part of the paper, through the organisation of concepts and their description within larger IT-related units (hardware, software, Internet). At the end of the paper, some proposals will be introduced in terms of possible IT training and education of translators, together with the conclusions and recommendations related to the topic.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Modeling in Three-Phase System and Frequency Domain Based on Kron Matrix Reduction
abstract: Analysis of harmonic propagation in transmission network represents an important factor in exploitation of the power system. These analyses are conducted in time and frequency domains. In a case of a robust power system, analyses are usually conducted in frequency domain and usually carried out in the Three-phase system (TPS), so that all effects of interest in the frequency spectrum are taken in consideration. Transmission line (TL) modeling in TPS and frequency domain, with the usage of Kron Matrix Reduction (KMR), can be found in this paper. The model is created for frequency values between 0.05 (Hz) and 10 (kHz), which represent the frequency spectrum of interest. Mathematical procedure for implementing the KMR can also be found in this paper. Usage of KMR for voltage profile analysis on a TL is shown on a plain example. The proposed model is compared with tested mathematical models from EMTP-RV.
